★ Base:- insurance is protection for all kinds of need & protection doesn't comes with cheap hands it does takes its price, 

• Examples👇
(a) Term Plan = Life Cover only meanwhile purest form of financial protection with the lowest cost and it doesn't promise to give any returns if you survive till the end of plan term(period of life cover),
But if wants to take maturity benefit then you "PAY EXTRA" to take Return of Premiums after taxes,
Meanwhile if you need Return you Pay Extra Premiums,

(b) Savings Plan (basically it divided in 3 categories:- Endowment/Lumpsum, only income/money back, income/money back + return of premium/maturity benefits)  👇
Base:- Life Cover + Maturity Benefit + All Taxes Benefit if you keep yearly premium below the 5 Lakhs, section 80C & 10(10D) even for Surrender Value, Death Benefit, Reduced Paid-up Policy Benefits.

It's just a very short overview.... There more details about....

• Term insurance is a real life insurance policy we can't compare it with any kind of Non-Participating Non-Linked individual life savings insurance policy..
Both are very different.
Term insurance is unavoidable.

• As per current market statistics all guaranteed return (product like nishchit aayush) plans have IRR (internal rate of return) in between 5% to 6.___% (something %) ,
If we are looking for investment purposes then it's avoidable to opt for this kind of plan ...

But if we are looking for a Regular but guaranteed money back from the end of 1st policy year with life cover (during the policy term) then it's okay to go with it (it's totally depend on an individual) with right policy term as per individual paying strength & planing.

• If an individual already has 1 Crore life cover and does not want to invest in mutual funds, market based investment option & eligible to have life cover for tax free maturity benefit then can go for it, IF okay with insurance company/like insurance company.
